translation.title: Terbinafine Hydrochloride Topical Solution
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for skin fungal infections caused by dermatophytes — athlete's foot (tinea pedis), jock itch (tinea cruris, ringworm of the groin) and ringworm of the body (tinea corporis) — and for pityriasis versicolor caused by Pityrosporum orbiculare.
translation.usage: Before use, wash the affected area clean and dry it completely, then apply enough of this medicine to the affected area 1 to 2 times a day so that the area and its surroundings are thoroughly wetted. The treatment period is once a day for 1 week for athlete's foot, jock itch and ringworm of the body, and twice a day for 1 week for pityriasis versicolor. Symptoms usually start to ease within 2 to 3 days; to prevent the infection from coming back, treat regularly with this medicine for the appropriate period.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you are breastfeeding, or in infants and children. Before using it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have lesions that alcohol may irritate. This medicine is for external use only. Do not use it in the eyes, on the cornea or conjunctiva; if it gets into the eyes, rinse them out completely with plenty of water. Do not use it on the face, nails, scalp, around the mouth or on the vaginal area, and use caution on cracked or eroded (raw, oozing) areas. Do not use an occlusive dressing or wrapping unless directed by a doctor. If the symptoms do not improve after the treatment period, consult a doctor or pharmacist. Stop use immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if adverse reactions occur, such as excessive irritation, hypersensitivity reactions, eye irritation, skin peeling, itching, skin lesions, hives, dry skin, contact dermatitis, eczema, a rash, pain, or pain or irritation at the application site.
